name: Vulnerability signals strength only when you cannot be wrecked by disclosure
definition: The strongest people are okay showing vulnerability because the implication is: you cannot wreck me even if you know my weaknesses. However, this is domain-specific. Where you're already ahead (speaker with friends in third-world country), vulnerability reinforces strength. Where you're behind or building authority (speaker on CT/Twitter where people make millions), the same vulnerability may undermine the authority you're trying to build. Being open about beliefs also functions as a self-screening mechanism: polarizing views attract aligned people and repel others, helping you find your tribe.
core_claim: If you show vulnerability from a position of established strength, then it signals confidence because the implication is they can't wreck you anyway. But if you show vulnerability while trying to build authority where you're behind others, then it may undermine that authority because the frame is different—you're trying to be taken seriously, not just be authentic.

idea_origin.event_summary: Speaker is very open/vulnerable with friends in real life (where he's ahead) but not online/Twitter/CT (where he's behind top performers). Talks about losing $24,000 to friends without shame, but dreads sharing this on CT where people would mock him.
idea_origin.trigger: Noticing the disconnect: 'I'd rather be understood and disliked than misunderstood and liked' works in real life but feels dangerous online. Masterful Lover community: went to improve, didn't care what they thought, became authority later. Twitter: the point IS to build authority, so caring matters.
idea_origin.lesson_learned: Vulnerability is strength is domain-specific. It works where you're already the big shark. It's risky where you're behind and trying to build authority. The mechanism is: vulnerability implies 'you can't wreck me'—but that only holds when you actually can't be wrecked.

canonical_instruction: Identify if the user is considering being vulnerable. Check their position in that domain: are they ahead (established, respected) or behind (newcomer, building authority)? If ahead, vulnerability signals strength because the implication is 'you can't wreck me.' If behind and trying to build authority, warn that vulnerability may undermine credibility before it's established. Distinguish between contexts where the goal is authenticity (improvement, connection) vs authority-building (perception matters). Note that openness about beliefs also self-screens for aligned people.

audiences: people deciding what to share publicly
people who are vulnerable in some contexts but not others
situations: deciding whether to share failures publicly
different comfort with vulnerability online vs offline
wanting to be authentic while building authority
exclusions: contexts where vulnerability is always inappropriate (hostile negotiations)
situations where position is irrelevant (pure support contexts)

transformation_rules: Identify the domain where user wants to be vulnerable
Assess user's position: ahead (big shark) or behind (building authority)?
If ahead, vulnerability signals 'you can't wreck me'—green light
If behind and building authority, warn that vulnerability may undermine before credibility is established
Distinguish: is the goal authenticity/improvement or authority-building?
Note that polarizing openness self-screens for aligned people (tribe-finding)
tests: Output distinguishes between vulnerability-from-strength vs vulnerability-while-building
Output identifies user's relative position in the specific domain
Output mentions the mechanism: vulnerability implies 'you can't wreck me'
No generic 'just be authentic' advice without position assessment
Output acknowledges that caring about perception is rational when building authority
Preserves the $24,000 loss example or equivalent contrast
counterexamples: Pure support contexts where position is irrelevant
Hostile negotiations where any vulnerability is exploited
Anonymous contexts where reputation cost is zero
input_triggers: comfortable being vulnerable with friends but not online
afraid to share losses or failures publicly
feeling like a big shark locally but small globally
wanting to be authentic while building authority
wondering whether to document the journey with failures included
polarizing beliefs that might repel some audiences
different levels of openness in different contexts
losing $24,000 and wondering whether to share it

related.note: High self-esteem traits include transparency and vulnerability-as-strength
Boundary talks require vulnerability (being open about what you didn't like)
Domain-specificity of vulnerability parallels stable vs dynamic domain distinction

components.name: Vulnerability from strength implies 'you can't wreck me'
components.applies_when: User is already ahead/established in the domain where they want to be vulnerable

components.name: Vulnerability while building authority may undermine before credibility is established
components.applies_when: User is behind others in the domain and trying to build authority, not just be authentic

components.name: Prefer understood-and-disliked over misunderstood-and-liked
components.applies_when: Meaningful communication where being understood matters more than being liked

components.name: Openness about beliefs self-screens for aligned people (tribe-finding)
components.applies_when: Polarizing views attract similar people and repel dissimilar ones

components.name: Masking or deflecting signals lack of boundaries or ownership
components.applies_when: Someone hides their views or deflects rather than owning their position
